topPRs.title: feat(cloud): persist subscription lifecycle and allowance authority
topPRs.author: wtfsayo
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- persist provider-neutral subscription lifecycle aggregates with immutable revision history
- project organization entitlements from the canonical immutable plan catalog
- add durable checkout/change/cancel command recovery, event receipts, deletion fences, and incidents
- persist exact allowance periods, funding reservations, source allocations, and append-only allowance ledger entries
- keep successful checkout fenced until its provider result is linked to durable lifecycle authority

This establishes the persistence and recovery authority for #23091. Live metered debit orchestration remains scoped to #23092; this PR does not change existing purchased-credit debit callers or activate Stripe workflows.

Closes #23091

## Adversarial review

The design and implementation went through five adversarial rounds covering scope ownership, module boundaries, provider uncertainty/recovery, purchased-credit coexistence, migration/concurrency safety, and final PR readiness. Two independent final reviewers then iterated on the concrete diff until both reported zero confirmed blockers.

Review-driven fixes included database-time webhook leases, authoritative provider-object retrieval semantics instead of fake Stripe versions, coherent historical replay, immutable-catalog entitlement derivation, pre-subscription checkout commands, checkout crash-window fencing, digest-bound result linkage, cancellation accounting guards, and real repository concurrency coverage.

## Verification

Passing:

- `bun install`
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared typecheck`
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared lint`
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared db:check-migrations`
- focused subscription/schema/migration/account-deletion suite: 48 passed, 0 failed
- real PostgreSQL 16 integration suite: 1 passed, 0 failed, 9 assertions
  - simultaneous checkout: one admitted, one rejected
  - overlapping allowance periods: one admitted, one rejected
  - last-dollar reserve through `SubscriptionAllowanceRepository`: one success, one conflict, exactly one reservation/allocation/ledger row
  - reserve blocked behind the organization lock crosses expiry and rolls back without balance or funding mutation
- `git diff --check`

Repository-wide `bun run verify` reached 375/376 tasks after dependency installation, then stopped in the unrelated UI molecular-inventory gate because its generated JSON/Markdown artifacts are stale. No UI files are touched here, so those unrelated generated artifacts were not rewritten or included.

The full cloud-shared suite also currently stops in the pre-existing dormant backup/restore API-boundary inventory test (`acquireAgentBackupRestoreLease must remain definition-only`); the focused changed contracts above pass.

## Evidence applicability

- UI screenshots/video/frontend logs: N/A — no rendered surface changed
- live Stripe calls: N/A — provider integration is deliberately not activated by this persistence PR
- live mixed allowance/purchased-credit debits: N/A — caller orchestration remains #23092
- model trajectories: N/A — no model behavior changed

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): isolate Dedicated startup from Shared runtime
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- remove the pending/provisioning Dedicated bootstrap path from the Shared Worker
- admit and cache only execution_tier=shared agents in Shared resolution
- make the app bridge and character routes report Dedicated unavailable until its real sandbox is running
- preserve the primary managed-Dedicated lifecycle failure and expose only allowlisted failure categories
- document the complete Shared, Dedicated, handoff, database, Hetzner, and warm-pool architecture

## Why

A signed-in Dedicated agent in a non-running lifecycle state could be served by the Shared Worker. That hid control-plane startup failures and violated the product boundary: signed-in app/cloud sessions must use Dedicated; Shared is reserved for public Eliza surfaces and connectors.

The latest staging canary (run 33280890733) proved that hosting capacity is no longer blocked by the earlier 402, but its provision job failed before container, database, heartbeat, mesh, or chat readiness. Cleanup then overwrote the original failure in evidence. This change makes the boundary fail closed and retains a privacy-safe provisioning category for the next live diagnostic.

Warm-pool enablement remains unchanged and false; the cold-start path must be correct first.

## Verification

- bun install --frozen-lockfile
- focused Shared resolver, Dedicated isolation, billing, REST adapter, canary, and workflow tests: 140 passing
- bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared typecheck
- bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared lint
- targeted Biome checks
- git diff --check
- bun run verify: 375/375 Turbo tasks plus all repository audit gates passing

Refs #29341

# Relates to

Closes #23107 (bounded first tranche as claimed in the issue thread: durable provider-neutral installation state machine in `@elizaos/core`, connector contribution contract types, Discord pilot adapter).

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop`
      with zero conflicts (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/develop`).
- [ ] `bun install` and `bun run verify` were run after sync, or any failure is
      recorded below with the exact unrelated blocker.
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the change works without reading the code, from the
      evidence attached below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased/merged onto the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts (base `7099dd568a`; merge-tree re-checked against the fresh upstream tip at publish time: 0 conflicts, no upstream commits touching the changed paths).
- [ ] `bun run verify` passes post-sync — full-repo verify not run in the contribution sandbox; focused gates below all pass at the exact head.

# Risks

Medium. Adds a new core service (`InstallationLifecycleService`) and connector contribution surface, but all wiring is opt-in: the Discord adapter registers the contribution and fences message traffic, while every other surface is untouched. Traffic fence is deliberately fail-open for scopes with no installation record (existing installs keep working); only terminal-state records (`removed`/`revoked`/`failed`) stop traffic, which is exactly the issue criterion ("removal stops traffic"). Scope-creep guard: no database migration, no API routes, no UI changes.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Implements the first tranche of the canonical invite-to-ready group installation lifecycle (#23107):

1. **Durable provider-neutral state machine** (`packages/core/src/messaging/installation-lifecycle.ts`): an account-scoped installation record joining provider invite, external group, required scopes, single-use expiring owner claim, runtime room binding, readiness state, removal, and reinstall versioning. States: `invite_created → provider_authorized → agent_joined → permissions_verifying → owner_claim_pending → ready`, with terminal `degraded`/`removed`/`revoked`/`failed`. Signed-event normalization: events are tenant-bound, idempotent, replay-safe (terminal receipt replay is a no-op), and epoch-guarded (future `reinstallVersion` epochs rejected; stale epochs rejected; equal-epoch reapply rejects wrong-secret attempts and persists attempt burning to exhaustion).
2. **Connector contribution contract** (`packages/core/src/messaging/installation-contribution.ts` + `installation-service.ts`): the contract a connector implements — install/deep-link shape, group types, scope requirements, signed event normalization, readiness proof, uninstall, provider-specific activation. `InstallationLifecycleService` registers contributions per `(agentId, connectorId)`.
3. **Discord pilot adapter** (`plugins/plugin-discord/installation-adapter.ts`, `discord-events.ts`, `index.ts`, `messages.ts`): canonical permission catalog (tiered invite URL activation), guildCreate/guildDelete normalization (unknown shapes refused), owner-claim handoff that never exposes tokens in the group, and the gateway-boundary fence — a fenced (removed/revoked/failed) guild skips `handleGuildCreate` at the event-listener seam and stops message traffic at the message-send seam.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (non-breaking change which adds functionality).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation (contract is documented in code headers; user-facing install UX arrives with the next tranche's install-URL surface).

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

1. `packages/core/src/messaging/installation-lifecycle.test.ts` — 49 tests over the state machine: legal transitions, replay/idempotency, claim single-use + expiry + attempt burning, epoch guards, removal semantics.
2. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-adapter.test.ts` — contribution shape (permission catalog, tiered invite URLs), event normalization (unknown shapes refused), traffic gate semantics.
3. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-gateway-boundary.test.ts` — the fence at the real `setupDiscordEventListeners` seam: a fenced guild never reaches `handleGuildCreate`.
4. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-contribution-init.test.ts` — plugin init registers the contribution against the real core service.

## Detailed testing steps

Run at the exact PR head (pinned bun 1.3.14):

```bash
bun test packages/core/src/messaging/installation-lifecycle.test.ts
# → 49 pass, 0 fail

npx vitest run --config plugins/plugin-discord/vitest.config.ts installation-adapter installation-contribution-init installation-gateway-boundary
# → 3 files, 23 tests, all pass
```

RED control (test discriminating power): reverting only the gateway-boundary fence in production code (pre-fence `fed1cc63a3`) makes the gateway-boundary suite fail 1/3 — the fence tests bite.

## Verification summary (exact head `9be613c5a3`)

- Core: 49/49 installation-lifecycle tests.
- Discord plugin: 23/23 across the three installation suites (adapter, contribution-init, gateway-boundary), via the plugin's own vitest config.
- Typecheck: clean (cloud-free scoped packages; re-verified after rebase onto `7099dd568a`).
- Biome: clean on all changed files (2 residual nits fixed in `9be613c5a3`).
- Merge-tree vs fresh upstream develop tip: 0 conflicts.
